objective: Add bounded version-compatible OPEN and CLOSE semantic actions addressed only by configured articulated-entity identifiers, while preserving the independent STOP, execution, observation, and verification boundaries.
decision_supported: Can Agent Runtime expose guarded articulated-entity open and close intent through the reviewed semantic contract without accepting raw motion, contact, geometry, or controller parameters?
acceptance: ActionType and the public SemanticAction JSON Schema register open and close while all existing action values and examples remain valid.
Each open or close action requires a non-empty opaque configured articulated-entity target_id.

The open and close parameter objects are closed and currently empty; callers cannot provide pose, trajectory, joint, velocity, acceleration, effort, force/torque, geometry, path, or arbitrary controller fields.
Pydantic construction and JSON ingress enforce the target and closed-parameter boundary, including strict rejection of unknown top-level fields.
The generated Schema Compiler model enforces the same conditional target and parameter constraints for both actions.
ToolRegistry registers both actions, requires their targets, rejects blank targets and forbidden parameters, and preserves independent STOP registration.
PolicyValidator accepts valid open and close actions and can require confirmation for either action without changing STOP behavior.

Execution-controller evidence forwards open and close intent without inventing motion parameters, reports adapter failures explicitly, and preserves queued STOP preemption at the next dispatch boundary.
A completed open or close ActionResult remains adapter execution evidence only and does not assert an observed articulated state or World Model verification.

The Task Packet boundary, focused tests, contract, scenario, context, full test, lint, and whitespace checks pass; interface changes remain subject to Runtime, World Model, Integration, and Motion owner review before merge.

stop_conditions: Implementation requires robot/control, Nav2, mapping, planners, fixture execution, firmware, hardware, or physical appliance changes.
A public parameter cannot remain closed and typed without exposing raw motion, contact, geometry, or controller details.
An executor would need to guess a generic articulated handle or claim observed state from ActionResult alone.
A required change falls outside allowed_paths or conflicts with an unrelated user worktree edit.
The interface change lacks the required Runtime, World Model, Integration, or Motion owner approval for merge.
A required validation command fails for a reason that cannot be fixed within this bounded contract and consumer scope.
risks_and_fallbacks: No articulated-entity catalog, handle geometry, force limit, or execution adapter is introduced; deployment configuration and unknown-target failure remain Motion-owned.
The empty parameter shape deliberately exposes no caller-controlled policy selector; any future closed selector set requires a separately reviewed contract change.
A successful adapter ActionResult remains distinct from post-action observation and World Model verification owned by #151 and related consumers.
Existing tabletop planners remain unchanged and continue emitting only their existing actions; appliance interaction skills belong to #160 after this contract is approved.
